raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

On Intel XPU, `_fwd_grouped_kernel_stage1` (TRITON_MLA decode) now loads its Q and Q-PE tiles through tensor descriptors instead of masked pointer loads, for the 576-wide MLA tile (`kv_lora_rank` 512 + `qk_rope_head_dim` 64) only. The K/V loop and the math are unchanged. The KV gather stays on pointer loads: this is a Q-tile change, not a descriptor path for the paged gather.

Context: RFC vllm-project/vllm#42545 recorded that this kernel could not use descriptors because of its paged KV gather. That still holds for K/V; the change here covers only the Q tile, which is a plain strided 2D tile, and only on XPU.

Scope: the gain applies to XPU runs that use `--attention-backend TRITON_MLA` explicitly, or that reach it as the fallback when `XPUFlashAttnMLABackend` rejects a config (`vllm/platforms/xpu.py`). The default XPU MLA backend (FlashAttnMLA) is faster than TRITON_MLA even with this change, and it is not affected. End-to-end numbers are on one model (DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat); most are with `--attention-backend TRITON_MLA` forced, plus one real fallback configuration (`--block-size 16`, where FlashAttnMLA rejects the config). Fp8 KV was not measured end to end. CUDA and ROCm launch the unchanged kernel.

Not a duplicate: no open PR adds tensor descriptors to this kernel. 18 other open PRs touch `triton_decode_attention.py` or its test file. Those that change the same code:
- vllm-project/vllm#51861 (draft) rewrites the Q-PE load; after it lands the descriptors here (`shape=[q_head_num, Lk]`) must be rebuilt for the split Q / Q-PE layout.
- vllm-project/vllm#51685 lets TRITON_MLA take a native fp8 KV cache and an fp8 query; the descriptor path would then see an fp8 Q, which is not tested here.
- vllm-project/vllm#52019 changes the stage-1 launcher signature and call site.
- vllm-project/vllm#61068, vllm-project/vllm#60173, vllm-project/vllm#54013 change `num_stages` handling next to the gate.
- vllm-project/vllm#63795, vllm-project/vllm#63796, vllm-project/vllm#48605 add a sliding-window constexpr to the same kernel next to `USE_TD`.
- vllm-project/vllm#57094, vllm-project/vllm#62725, vllm-project/vllm#40705, vllm-project/vllm#63623, vllm-project/vllm#57902, vllm-project/vllm#52472, vllm-project/vllm#50629 touch other parts of the kernel file and/or append tests; vllm-project/vllm#64783 and vllm-project/vllm#64534 touch only the test file.

Whichever lands second needs a mechanical rebase.

## Claims

- On XPU, `VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD` unset (the default) or `1` loads the Q / Q-PE tiles of the 576/512 MLA tile (one KV head) through descriptors. `0` keeps the pointer load. Outputs are bit-identical to the pointer load. The 288/256 tile keeps the pointer load for now: with descriptors its kernel-level result is mixed (faster on 8 of 12 shapes, 5.2-6.5% slower on the other 4), and no 288/256 model was run end to end.
- On 2× Intel Arc Pro B60 (`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat`, TP=2, TRITON_MLA), the decode step is 4.3-6.0% faster at batch 1 and 17.7-24.0% faster at batch 8/32. Serve median TPOT drops by 4.4% / 17.7% / 22.2% at concurrency 1 / 8 / 32. gsm8k showed no significant difference (1 run per arm, see Accuracy).
- Per launch, the kernel is faster on all 24 bf16 and all 12 fp8-KV shapes of the 576/512 tile (table below, default arm).
- CUDA/ROCm: no behaviour change. The descriptor branch is a `tl.constexpr` that is always `False` there, and the gate checks the platform before reading the env var. `VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD=1` does not enable this path outside XPU.

## Validation

Software: image `vllm/vllm-openai-xpu@sha256:14d76deea7c2abab18ce13f0031c8fc765736a39bdd4252014fa1255b2c1db88` (vLLM `3966924d5`, torch 2.14.0+xpu, triton-xpu 3.8.0 as pinned in `requirements/xpu.txt`, IGC 2.38.2, compute-runtime 26.27.39122.11). The image's `triton_decode_attention.py` is byte-identical to `main` before this PR. Every run puts a copy of the measured revision of that file (and of the test file for pytest) first on `PYTHONPATH` (XPU) or over the image's install (CUDA).

Unit tests on the final revision (kernel file md5 `1e712614`, test file md5 `d6bcf8ac`):

```bash
env -u VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD pytest -v -rA --tb=short tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_decode_attention.py
VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD=0 pytest -v -rA --tb=short tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_decode_attention.py
VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD=1 pytest -v -rA --tb=short tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_decode_attention.py
```

| device | unset | `0` | `1` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1× Intel Arc Pro B60 | 132 passed, 1 skipped | 132 passed, 1 skipped | 132 passed, 1 skipped |
| 1× NVIDIA H200 (sm90) | 132 passed, 1 skipped | 132 passed, 1 skipped | 132 passed, 1 skipped |
| 1× NVIDIA B200 (sm100) | 132 passed, 1 skipped | 132 passed, 1 skipped | 132 passed, 1 skipped |

The skip is the fp8-KV non-MLA case, which is not wired. The tests ran from a directory without a `vllm/` source tree, with the kernel and test files imported from a copy (the printed `vllm.__file__` and file md5s were checked in every run).

ROCm was not run. `test_decode_attention_mla_tensor_descriptor` covers the 576/512 descriptor path (32 and 8 heads, bf16 and fp8 KV) and the pointer fallbacks (288/256, GQA, non-MLA, last stride != 1, row stride not 16-byte aligned, base pointer not 16-byte aligned; 15 passed and 1 skipped per run). A launch spy asserts that `tt.descriptor_load` appears in the compiled TTIR exactly when the descriptor path is selected, that the path equals "XPU and not `0`", and that the output equals the pointer load bit for bit. On CUDA, `=1` selects the pointer path (the test asserts it), so the CUDA columns show that the kernel is unchanged there; they do not validate the descriptor path. On H200 and B200, the TTIR, TTGIR and PTX of `_fwd_grouped_kernel_stage1` (line info stripped) are identical to `main` for five shapes at unset/0/1.

Kernel time on 1× Intel Arc Pro B60, kernel file of this PR. Measured with kernel file md5 `546fc408`, which differs from this PR's final file only in the gate (`Lk in (576, 288)` vs `Lk == 576`); the `@triton.jit` kernel is byte-identical, so the 576/512 rows apply as measured. Method: `torch.profiler` device time per launch, page 16, `num_kv_splits` as chosen by TRITON_MLA. Runs: 3 processes with a fresh Triton cache × 5 rounds, median of medians. Spread is (max-min)/median of the process medians, at most 8.3% and below 4% on most shapes. The TD arm is the shipped default (variable unset); baseline is TD `0`, which is within -0.1% (median) of `main`.

| tile (Lk/Lv) | KV | shapes (heads × batch 1/8/32 × context 1k/8k) | faster with TD | change vs TD `0` | median |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 576/512 | bf16 | 24 (heads 16/8/4/2) | 24/24 | -7.6% … -32.5% | -10.3% |
| 576/512 | fp8 e4m3 | 12 (heads 16/8) | 12/12 | -6.9% … -28.7% | -8.8% |

End to end on 2× Intel Arc Pro B60: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat` revision `85864749cd`, TP=2, bf16, bf16 KV, `--attention-backend TRITON_MLA`, `max_model_len=5120`, no prefix caching, seed 42, default XPU graphs. Only `VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD` differs between arms: `0` (pointer load) vs unset (the default, descriptor load). Arms run interleaved in the order 0, unset, unset, 0.

These runs used an earlier revision of the kernel file (https://github.com/afierka-intel/vllm/commit/6672eaf2d7); the final revision only narrows the gate to `Lk == 576`, which is the only shape this model uses. Compiling the stage-1 kernel with the earlier and the final file on the same B60 gives identical Triton cache keys for the TD-off arm (5 of 5 variants) and for the 4 descriptor variants of the unset arm; the fifth (288/256) is now a pointer variant with the TD-off key, as intended. So the 576/512 E2E rows below apply to the final file. The Triton cache of every `0` process holds only pointer variants of the kernel, and of every unset process only descriptor variants. `VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD=1` at input 4096, batch 8 gives a 157.1 ms decode step, the same as unset (157.5 ms).

Latency (output 256). Runs: 2 processes × 4 timed iterations after 1 warm-up = 8 values per arm. Batch 1 was repeated with 2 more processes per arm in BAAB order (4 processes per arm pooled): 1024 × 1: 22.7 -> 21.7 ms (-4.3%), 4096 × 1: 43.9 -> 41.1 ms (-6.3%); the 4 process medians per arm are separated, exact permutation p = 0.029 in both cases (smallest possible with 4 vs 4). Decode step = (latency at 256 output tokens - latency at 1 output token) / 255. Spread is (max-min)/median of the decode step.

| input | batch | latency s, TD `0` -> unset | decode step ms, TD `0` -> unset | change | spread `0` / unset |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 1 | 5.90 -> 5.65 | 22.7 -> 21.7 | -4.3% | 3.4% / 3.8% |
| 1024 | 8 | 22.80 -> 18.87 | 87.0 -> 71.6 | -17.7% | 3.7% / 4.4% |
| 1024 | 32 | 65.47 -> 51.34 | 248.0 -> 192.6 | -22.3% | 1.0% / 1.2% |
| 4096 | 1 | 11.49 -> 10.82 | 43.7 -> 41.1 | -6.0% | 2.3% / 2.9% |
| 4096 | 8 | 53.43 -> 42.54 | 200.2 -> 157.5 | -21.3% | 1.3% / 1.4% |
| 4096 | 32 (see note) | 188.07 -> 145.28 | 700.3 -> 532.5 | -24.0% | 1.5% / 1.0% |

Note on 4096 × 32: KV capacity is 91,488 tokens, so the engine ran 21-22 requests at a time (the rest waited); it is a valid A/B but not a batch-32 decode step.

Serve (random 1024 in / 256 out, `--ignore-eos`). Runs: 2 servers per arm × 2 runs after 1 warm-up = 4 values per arm. Every run completed all prompts.

| concurrency | prompts | median TPOT ms, TD `0` -> unset | change | output tok/s, TD `0` -> unset | change | spread TPOT `0` / unset |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 16 | 22.70 -> 21.71 | -4.4% | 43.1 -> 45.1 | +4.5% | 3.4% / 3.6% |
| 8 | 32 | 85.79 -> 70.64 | -17.7% | 90.6 -> 109.5 | +20.9% | 1.5% / 1.2% |
| 32 | 128 | 248.99 -> 193.77 | -22.2% | 126.1 -> 161.6 | +28.2% | 0.4% / 0.8% |

Accuracy: gsm8k, 5-shot, all 1319 questions, lm-eval 0.4.12, greedy, seed 42, TP=2 TRITON_MLA. 4 independent processes per arm (3 on the final kernel file, 1 earlier on the same Triton cache keys), TD `0` vs TD unset (this PR):

| arm | strict-match per process | mean (range) | flexible-extract mean (range) |
|---|---|---|---|
| TD `0` | 0.6634, 0.6626, 0.6588, 0.6664 | 66.28% (65.88-66.64) | 66.85% (66.49-67.32) |
| TD unset (this PR) | 0.6588, 0.6558, 0.6664, 0.6603 | 66.03% (65.58-66.64) | 66.72% (66.26-67.17) |
| FlashAttnMLA (default backend), TD unset, 1 process | 0.6641 | | 0.6702 |

Each process has stderr ±0.0130. The noise floor is measured with TD-off vs TD-off pairs: the strict-match difference between two processes is 0.00-1.06 pt (median 0.38) for TD `0` vs unset, 0.08-0.76 pt (median 0.38) for TD `0` vs TD `0`, and 0.15-1.06 pt (median 0.53) for unset vs unset. Paired exact McNemar p ≥ 0.12 for every one of the 28 process pairs, TD `0` vs TD `0` included. Identical generations out of 1319 are 674-752 for every pair, and no higher for TD `0` vs TD `0` than for TD `0` vs unset. So generations are not reproducible across processes on this setup, and the TD-vs-pointer difference is inside that run-to-run noise. This does not prove a zero drop; it shows none that is resolvable at this sample size.

Default XPU MLA backend vs TRITON_MLA, decode step ms (same job and setup; FlashAttnMLA: 1 process × 4 iterations):

| input × batch | FlashAttnMLA (default) | TRITON_MLA, TD `0` | TRITON_MLA, TD unset (this PR) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 × 8 | 23.9 | 87.0 | 71.6 |
| 4096 × 8 | 25.1 | 200.2 | 157.5 |

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands (E2E)</summary>

The latency and gsm8k numbers came from one process per arm. Each process ran the `vllm bench latency` loop for all six configs, plus lm-eval (Python API) on the same engine. The equivalent CLI commands are:

```bash
export VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD=0   # TD arm: unset VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD
M=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat
COMMON="--tensor-parallel-size 2 --attention-backend TRITON_MLA --max-model-len 5120 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --trust-remote-code --seed 42 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9"

# latency; repeat with --output-len 1 for the decode-step estimate
vllm bench latency --model $M $COMMON --input-len 4096 --output-len 256 --batch-size 8 \
  --num-iters-warmup 1 --num-iters 4

# serve
vllm serve $M --served-model-name dsv2lite $COMMON
vllm bench serve --model dsv2lite --tokenizer $M --trust-remote-code --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 256 --random-range-ratio 0 --ignore-eos \
  --num-prompts 32 --max-concurrency 8 --seed 42 --temperature 0

# accuracy
lm_eval --model vllm --model_args pretrained=$M,dtype=bfloat16,tensor_parallel_size=2,attention_backend=TRITON_MLA,max_model_len=5120,enable_prefix_caching=False,trust_remote_code=True,seed=42,gpu_memory_utilization=0.9 \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size auto --seed 42
```

</details>

CI gap: no CI job runs the descriptor path of this PR. `.buildkite/intel_jobs/kernels_intel.yaml` has no step for `tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_decode_attention.py`, and the CUDA (L4, sm89) and ROCm (MI300, `optional: true`) "Attention Kernels" steps run the file on the pointer path only. The XPU results above come from local runs. Intel CI: build 16275 of the previous head failed within 5 s without running any job; the build for the current head was pending when this was written.

Fallback configuration (no `--attention-backend`, `--block-size 16`): the engine log shows `FlashAttnMLA on XPU is not valid for this configuration (('block_size not supported',)); falling back to Triton MLA backend`. Same model, flags and methodology as above, arms interleaved 0, unset, unset, 0 (decode step: 1 process per arm-slot, 2 per arm):

| input | batch | decode step ms, TD `0` -> unset | change | process medians `0` / unset |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 1 | 22.7 -> 22.3 | -2.0% | 22.4, 23.0 / 22.3, 22.3 |
| 1024 | 8 | 87.2 -> 73.1 | -16.1% | 86.5, 87.4 / 73.2, 73.0 |
| 4096 | 1 | 43.9 -> 41.6 | -5.4% | 43.4, 44.2 / 41.6, 41.5 |
| 4096 | 8 | 199.9 -> 158.2 | -20.9% | 199.6, 200.9 / 158.5, 158.1 |

(The 1024 × 8 unset spread of 42.3% is a single outlier iteration; both process medians are 73.0-73.2 ms.) Serve, same setup (4 values per arm, all prompts completed): median TPOT 22.75 -> 21.73 ms (-4.5%) at concurrency 1, 85.79 -> 70.82 ms (-17.5%) at 8, 248.70 -> 193.90 ms (-22.0%) at 32. fp8 KV is the other fallback case and was not measured end to end (next paragraph).

fp8 KV: covered by the unit tests only. End to end, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` does not run on XPU today, for a reason unrelated to this PR: the MLA layer passes `skip_scale=True` when the checkpoint has no KV scales, and `concat_and_cache_mla` raises `NotImplementedError("skip_scale is not supported on XPU")`.

## Details

- **Why it is faster:** on XPU, the masked pointer load of the 16 × 512 Q tile lowers to an SLM relayout (288 SLM `d16u32` loads in the 576/512 kernel). The descriptor load lowers to 18 2D block reads that land directly in the DPAS operand layout, and the relayout disappears (288/256: 9 block reads, 144 SLM loads removed). With TP=2 on DeepSeek-V2-Lite, stage 1 is 83-87% of decode device time at input 4096 with batch 8/32, and its per-launch time drops from 8.08 ms to 6.08 ms at input 4096, batch 8 (`torch.profiler`, eager).
- **Gate:** `is_xpu() and is_mla and Lk == 576 and kv_group_num == head_num and use_tensor_descriptor()`, plus a unit last stride and 16-byte-aligned base and strides of `q`. The platform check comes first, so CUDA/ROCm do no env lookup. `use_tensor_descriptor()` supplies the `VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD` tri-state (unset: on for XPU, `0`: off), as in vllm-project/vllm#46340 and vllm-project/vllm#47205. Unlike those, this kernel's descriptor path is XPU-only: `1` does not force it on CUDA/ROCm, where it has not been validated. `vllm/envs.py` is not changed.
- **Masking:** with one KV head, the kernel's row mask reduces to `row < q_head_num`, and the descriptor's bounds pad exactly those rows with zeros. `BLOCK_DMODEL` is below `Lk`, so the column mask is all-true, and the Q-PE descriptor starts at column `BLOCK_DMODEL`. That is why the results match bit for bit. Descriptor loads take no `.ca` cache hint.
- **No allocator needed:** every XPU descriptor build here has `global_scratch_size = 0`, so no `triton.set_allocator` call is added.
- **Tradeoffs and limits:**
  - The 288/256 tile is mixed with descriptors: faster on 8 of 12 shapes (batch 1 at 1k and 8k context, batch 8/32 at 1k context), 5.2-6.5% slower on the other 4 (batch 8/32 at 8k context), and no 288/256 model was run end to end. It is left out of the gate until the slowdown is understood.
  - Only Intel Arc Pro B60 was measured; B70 and B580 were not.
  - The kernel spills about 98 KB on XPU in both paths. The descriptor load does not change that (576/512: 97,920 B vs 99,584 B).
  - Tuning `num_warps` (2/4/8) and the GRF mode did not beat the pointer path's gain from this change, and did not improve the descriptor path beyond `num_warps=4`.
  - gsm8k generations are not reproducible across processes on this setup even with the same compiled kernel (see Accuracy for the measured TD-off vs TD-off noise floor).
- AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this change and this description.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [ ] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.

CI gap: no CI job runs the descriptor path of this PR. `.buildkite/intel_jobs/kernels_intel.yaml` has no step for `tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_decode_attention.py`, and the CUDA (L4, sm89) and ROCm (MI300, `optional: true`) "Attention Kernels" steps run the file on the pointer path only. The XPU results above come from local runs. Intel CI: build 16275 of the previous head failed within 5 s without running any job; the build for the current head was pending when this was written.

Fallback configuration (no `--attention-backend`, `--block-size 16`): the engine log shows `FlashAttnMLA on XPU is not valid for this configuration (('block_size not supported',)); falling back to Triton MLA backend`. Same model, flags and methodology as above, arms interleaved 0, unset, unset, 0 (decode step: 1 process per arm-slot, 2 per arm):

| input | batch | decode step ms, TD `0` -> unset | change | process medians `0` / unset |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 1 | 22.7 -> 22.3 | -2.0% | 22.4, 23.0 / 22.3, 22.3 |
| 1024 | 8 | 87.2 -> 73.1 | -16.1% | 86.5, 87.4 / 73.2, 73.0 |
| 4096 | 1 | 43.9 -> 41.6 | -5.4% | 43.4, 44.2 / 41.6, 41.5 |
| 4096 | 8 | 199.9 -> 158.2 | -20.9% | 199.6, 200.9 / 158.5, 158.1 |

(The 1024 × 8 unset spread of 42.3% is a single outlier iteration; both process medians are 73.0-73.2 ms.) Serve, same setup (4 values per arm, all prompts completed): median TPOT 22.75 -> 21.73 ms (-4.5%) at concurrency 1, 85.79 -> 70.82 ms (-17.5%) at 8, 248.70 -> 193.90 ms (-22.0%) at 32. fp8 KV is the other fallback case and was not measured end to end (next paragraph).

fp8 KV: covered by the unit tests only. End to end, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` does not run on XPU today, for a reason unrelated to this PR: the MLA layer passes `skip_scale=True` when the checkpoint has no KV scales, and `concat_and_cache_mla` raises `NotImplementedError("skip_scale is not supported on XPU")`.

## Details

- **Why it is faster:** on XPU, the masked pointer load of the 16 × 512 Q tile lowers to an SLM relayout (288 SLM `d16u32` loads in the 576/512 kernel). The descriptor load lowers to 18 2D block reads that land directly in the DPAS operand layout, and the relayout disappears (288/256: 9 block reads, 144 SLM loads removed). With TP=2 on DeepSeek-V2-Lite, stage 1 is 83-87% of decode device time at input 4096 with batch 8/32, and its per-launch time drops from 8.08 ms to 6.08 ms at input 4096, batch 8 (`torch.profiler`, eager).
- **Gate:** `is_xpu() and is_mla and Lk == 576 and kv_group_num == head_num and use_tensor_descriptor()`, plus a unit last stride and 16-byte-aligned base and strides of `q`. The platform check comes first, so CUDA/ROCm do no env lookup. `use_tensor_descriptor()` supplies the `VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD` tri-state (unset: on for XPU, `0`: off), as in vllm-project/vllm#46340 and vllm-project/vllm#47205. Unlike those, this kernel's descriptor path is XPU-only: `1` does not force it on CUDA/ROCm, where it has not been validated. `vllm/envs.py` is not changed.
- **Masking:** with one KV head, the kernel's row mask reduces to `row < q_head_num`, and the descriptor's bounds pad exactly those rows with zeros. `BLOCK_DMODEL` is below `Lk`, so the column mask is all-true, and the Q-PE descriptor starts at column `BLOCK_DMODEL`. That is why the results match bit for bit. Descriptor loads take no `.ca` cache hint.
- **No allocator needed:** every XPU descriptor build here has `global_scratch_size = 0`, so no `triton.set_allocator` call is added.
- **Tradeoffs and limits:**
  - The 288/256 tile is mixed with descriptors: faster on 8 of 12 shapes (batch 1 at 1k and 8k context, batch 8/32 at 1k context), 5.2-6.5% slower on the other 4 (batch 8/32 at 8k context), and no 288/256 model was run end to end. It is left out of the gate until the slowdown is understood.
  - Only Intel Arc Pro B60 was measured; B70 and B580 were not.
  - The kernel spills about 98 KB on XPU in both paths. The descriptor load does not change that (576/512: 97,920 B vs 99,584 B).
  - Tuning `num_warps` (2/4/8) and the GRF mode did not beat the pointer path's gain from this change, and did not improve the descriptor path beyond `num_warps=4`.
  - gsm8k generations are not reproducible across processes on this setup even with the same compiled kernel (see Accuracy for the measured TD-off vs TD-off noise floor).
- AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this change and this description.

+class _GroupedStage1Spy:
+    """Records USE_TD and the TTIR of each grouped stage-1 launch."""
+
+    def __init__(self, kernel):
+        self.kernel = kernel
+        self.launches: list[tuple[bool, str]] = []
+
+    def __getitem__(self, grid):
+        launch = self.kernel[grid]
+
+        def run(*args, **kwargs):
+            compiled = launch(*args, **kwargs)
+            self.launches.append((kwargs["USE_TD"], compiled.asm["ttir"]))
+            return compiled
+
+        return run
+
+
+def _make_q(layout, B, H_Q, D_QK, dtype):
+    """Q with a given memory layout; all variants hold the same values."""
+    q = torch.randn(B, H_Q, D_QK, dtype=dtype, device=DEVICE_TYPE)
+    if layout == "contiguous":
+        return q
+    if layout == "stride_last_not_1":
+        # (B, H_Q, D_QK) view with stride(-1) == H_Q
+        return q.transpose(1, 2).contiguous().transpose(1, 2)
+    if layout == "row_stride_unaligned":
+        # stride(1) = D_QK + 1 elements: not a multiple of 16 bytes
+        return torch.randn(B, H_Q, D_QK + 1, dtype=dtype, device=DEVICE_TYPE)[
+            ..., :D_QK
+        ]
+    if layout == "base_unaligned":
+        # base pointer one element (2 bytes) past a 16-byte boundary
+        buf = torch.randn(B * H_Q * D_QK + 8, dtype=dtype, device=DEVICE_TYPE)
+        return buf[1 : 1 + B * H_Q * D_QK].view(B, H_Q, D_QK)
+    raise AssertionError(layout)
+

+def test_decode_attention_mla_tensor_descriptor(

+    576-wide MLA tile with a 16-byte-aligned unit-stride Q, on XPU, unless
+    VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD=0.  It gives the same bits as the pointer load: only
+    the Q load differs, the math is unchanged."""
+    if kv_dtype != torch.bfloat16 and not is_mla:
